extracted.intended_audience: Director of Central Intelligence and Intelligence Community leadership / policymakers considering application of OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: An internal intelligence-community memorandum arguing why draft OMB Circular A-76 (performance of commercial activities) cannot be applied to certain intelligence activities and requesting a community-wide exemption; it documents policy conflicts, operational examples, and proposed next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB A-76: Prohibition on in-house justification based on strike or classified program
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular's current policy states that 'activities may not be justified for in-house operation on the basis that (1) there is a possibility of a strike by contract employees, [or] (2) the activity involves or supports a classified program.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memo notes that during the recent revision no change was made to this policy; CIA has not been participating in the A-76 program because the policy precludes citing classified-program protection or strike possibility as reasons for keeping functions in-house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of intelligence sources and methods as a basis for exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone in the Intelligence Community shares the responsibility to protect intelligence sources and methods, and the community should adopt a consistent position on what would permit fulfilling that responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSA argues that protecting sensitive intelligence material is a valid ground to seek relief from A-76 requirements; the memo enlists support for seeking a community-wide exemption to preserve ability to protect sources/methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public exposure and lack of procedural flexibility under A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: The public exposure and lack of flexibility inherent in the A-76 program would not permit adequate protection of sensitive intelligence material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSA acknowledges endorsement of A-76 general policies when practical but stresses that the transparency and procedural constraints of the A-76 competitive/public processes create unacceptable risks to classified operations and information.

rubrics_metrics.name: User acceptance and operational feasibility (example: DOE communications center)
rubrics_metrics.description: If contractor operation of a facility would cause essential users to discontinue use or withhold data (e.g., discontinuing electrical transmission of intelligence), contracting is operationally unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memo cites Department of Energy's aborted plan to contract operation of its all-source communications center: users including CIA threatened to stop transmissions if contractors ran the facility, forcing DOE to cancel—used as concrete evidence that user acceptance must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek community-wide exemption for intelligence activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A coordinated Intelligence Community position and action are necessary to obtain relief from A-76 requirements for activities where compliance would compromise intelligence responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSA requests support in seeking community-wide exemption and offers staff assistance and a point-of-contact to work with representatives on the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional endorsement of contracting where practical, economical, and appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The NSA relies on the private sector to provide goods and services 'whenever practical, economical, and appropriate' and endorses the general policies espoused in OMB Circular A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memo balances its request for exemption by acknowledging that contracting is acceptable under the usual practical/economic/appropriateness criteria, but not where A-76's transparency/flexibility constraints threaten security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional concerns about unlimited contract operation
rubrics_metrics.description: During the revision, provisions were made to accommodate congressional concerns about unlimited contract operation of certain services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memo notes these revisions but points out they did not change the policy forbidding use of classified-program protection or strike possibility as justification for in-house operation, leaving a gap for intelligence needs.
